name: rtxspark
description: An RTX Spark-class laptop SoC GPU: the RTX 5080's Blackwell SM (rtx5080), 48 of them, on 273 GB/s of unified LPDDR5X. A study shape, not a calibrated part: the clock, the L2 and every latency are the RTX 5080's.

sources.NUM_CORES: 6,144 CUDA cores in the top configuration (NVIDIA RTX Spark specifications), taken as 48 SMs of 128 FP32 lanes like the other Blackwell parts
sources.PLATFORM_MEMORY_NUM_BANKS, PLATFORM_MEMO: A 256-bit LPDDR5X-8533 interface: 16 16-bit channels x 2 B x 8533 MT/s = 273 GB/s, the reported effective bandwidth (NVIDIA quotes 300 GB/s). The simulators have no LPDDR5X timing, so the channels run the GDDR6 model at this data rate, as rtx5080 runs GDDR7
sources.SM (all core knobs), L2, PLATFORM_CLOCK_: Inherited from rtx5080 unchanged. None is published for this part: the laptop clock is lower, the L2 is likely smaller, and the memory is shared with the CPU through the SoC's memory subsystem
sources.reference: fp32_lanes is the vendor CUDA core count; dram_bandwidth_gbs the reported effective bandwidth. No latency reference: nothing here is measured on the part
